baseline.note:
Chief Complaint: Intermittent tight chest sensation for 3 days, precipitated by exertion (walking up a hill), lasting a few minutes and relieved by rest.

History of Present Illness: Chest tightness associated with mild dyspnea; occasional radiation to left arm; no jaw pain reported. No associated diaphoresis or palpitations. No current pain at exam.

Past Medical History: Hypertension, on amlodipine 5 mg daily.

Social History: Smokes ~10 cigarettes per day. No alcohol or drug use mentioned.

Family History: Father had myocardial infarction at age 52; brother with hypercholesterolemia.

Allergies: Penicillin (rash).

Review of Systems: Negative except for described chest discomfort and mild shortness of breath during episodes.

Physical Examination: BP 152/94 mmHg, HR 88 regular, heart sounds normal, lungs clear, no peripheral edema.

Assessment: Likely exertional angina versus non‑cardiac chest pain; risk factors include hypertension, smoking, family history of premature CAD.

Plan: Obtain ECG today; consider further cardiac work‑up (stress test, lipid panel) based on results; counsel smoking cessation; optimize blood pressure control; advise to seek immediate care if pain becomes persistent, radiates to jaw, or is accompanied by sweating or syncope.
